summary: Draft Control Power record. `TtmEnabled` sits under `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power`, has an exact repo-doc default of `0`, exists on the observed clean baseline with preview value `0`, produced an exact current-build Unicode string hit in `ntoskrnl.exe`, and later gained a lightweight public-header corroboration through `systeminformer/phnt` where `ntpoapi.h` exposes `BOOLEAN TtmEnabled;`. A later current-build INIT-table follow-up also showed `TtmEnabled` adjacent to the broader `Power` descriptor family that contains the execution-required pair and Power Throttling surfaces. The main caution is runtime behavior: a dedicated mega-trigger isolation pass later showed `DWORD=1` reproducing `boot-unsafe` on the pilot-safe profile. That is enough for a schema-backed draft, but not for a safe tweak recommendation.

setting.name: TTM Enabled
setting.casual_explanation: TtmEnabled is a low-level Control\Power registry value tied to an internal `TtmpEnabled` power-manager state.
setting.why_people_change_it: Researchers track it when studying low-level power-manager behavior, adjacent execution-required settings, and boot-sensitive Control\Power toggles.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The lane has exact repo docs, a clean baseline value, a current-build `ntoskrnl.exe` string hit, a public-header corroboration through `systeminformer/phnt`, and adjacency inside the broader current-build Power init-table family. The same lane also has a strong red flag: an isolated runtime probe with `DWORD=1` reproduced `boot-unsafe`, so the value is currently research-only and unsuitable for any apply surface.
setting.professional_notes: The kernel-power 96 routing pass grouped TtmEnabled inside the main `Control\Power` docs cluster. The clean phase-0 existence batch later confirmed that `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Power\TtmEnabled` exists on the Win25H2Clean baseline with preview value `0`. The broad targeted string batch then found an exact Unicode hit for `TtmEnabled` in `C:\Windows\System32\ntoskrnl.exe`. A later source-enrichment follow-up over a shallow `winsiderss/systeminformer` clone surfaced `BOOLEAN TtmEnabled;` in `phnt/include/ntpoapi.h`, which is not a primary Microsoft contract but does corroborate that the value family remains visible through a public NT-style header surface. A later host-side INIT-table follow-up for the execution-required pair also showed `TtmEnabled` adjacent to the broader current-build `Power` descriptor slice, which strengthens that this is a real member of the same initialization family rather than a stray doc-only token. The main runtime result is negative for safety: the mega-trigger V2 follow-up isolated `TtmEnabled` under `DWORD=1` and recorded `boot-unsafe`, while sibling `HiberbootEnabled` and `MSDisabled` probes on the same pilot-safe family stayed individually safe. That means the record is strong enough for schema-backed tracking, but not for a user-facing or bench-ready apply lane.
